Question: Three machines \(P,\) \(Q,\) and \(R,\) working together, can do a job in \(x\) hours. When working alone, \(P\) needs an additional \(6\) hours to do the job; \(Q,\) one additional hour; and \(R,\) \(x\) additional hours. The value of \(x\) is:
Solution:
Work rates add when the machines operate together. Take the whole job as \(1\) unit and require \(x>0\). The solo completion times for \(P,Q,R\) are \(x+6\), \(x+1\), and \(2x\) hours, respectively, so
\[
\frac1{x+6}+\frac1{x+1}+\frac1{2x}=\frac1x.
\]
Machine \(R\) supplies half the combined rate. Subtracting its rate leaves
\[
\frac1{x+6}+\frac1{x+1}=\frac1{2x}.
\]
All denominators are positive for \(x>0\), so multiplying by \(2x(x+6)(x+1)\) is valid. This gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
2x(2x+7)&=(x+6)(x+1),\\
3x^2+7x-6&=0,\\
(3x-2)(x+3)&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The candidates are \(x=\frac23\) and \(x=-3\); the negative value cannot represent elapsed time. At \(x=\frac23\), the solo rates are \(\frac3{20},\frac35,\frac34\) jobs per hour, whose sum is \(\frac32=1/x\). Thus the valid answer is \(\frac23\) hour, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
